title: a fresh sport steering wheel
lensAText: a sceptical automotive interior art director. Look at every frame the builder cites (before and after) with the Read tool, then take your own in ONE short Playwright script on dist/artifact.html: the seat view (setCam('cockpit')) of the Rossini GT and the OC Hypercar at 390x844 (a copy of dist/artifact.html with <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover"> injected; isMobile, hasTouch, DPR 3) at Night and 1280x720 Day, while driving with a little steering, and switch the handling profile once to see the left dial change. Judge: does it read, at phone size, as a fresh modern premium sport wheel (Alcantara, carbon, flat bottom, stitching, stripe, the dial widgets and thumb pads)? Is it well made (no gaps, z-fighting, floating parts, hands clipping or floating, blurry or unreadable dials)? Is it OUR OWN design with no real brand's name, logo or copied shape?
brief: THE OWNER (2026-11-09 ~noon PT): "Make sure the steering wheel is updated and looks all fresh like the AMG Alcanatra Carbon Fiber sports steering wheel Mercedes has with the button widgets attached too". Build OUR OWN design in that style family (modern premium sport wheels), never a copy of any real maker's wheel: no AMG, Mercedes or other real brand names, logos, stars, badges or their exact shapes and button layouts anywhere. The cockpit's steering wheel is built in src/preview/cockpit.ts (per-car via THEMES; the game builds it through src/game/vehicle/PlayerCar.ts buildCockpit); new parts may live in a helper such as src/preview/wheel-sport.ts. Use the new sport wheel on the Rossini GT (default car), the Rossini Corsa and the OC Hypercar, each in its own trim (GT: black Alcantara grips, cognac stitching, carbon top and bottom; Corsa: Alcantara with the yellow stripe; Hypercar: Alcantara with ice-blue stitching and stripe). The Brio and the Vela E keep their own character but get the same thumb pads. Must have: a flat bottom made by the bottom trim ONLY away from the grips; 2x2 twill carbon under clear coat top and bottom with crisp joins; Alcantara grips with double contrast stitching and a 12 o'clock stripe; slim spokes in gloss black and brushed metal; on each lower spoke a rotary dial widget (knurled ring around a small round colour display, lit at night) plus a small button, and two thumb pads on the upper spokes; the dial displays are canvas textures showing LIVE state (left: handling profile Arcade/Sport/Sim; right: hypercar Thrust tank and tune, others TCS or gear), redrawn only when the value changes; brushed paddles; shift lights kept where the car had them; the car's own badge (R, V or OC mark) on the hub. HARD LIMITS: do NOT change src/preview/spec.ts or the rim path/cross-section where the hands hold it (GRIP at 32 and 148 degrees, about +-16 degrees) so the hands still sit exactly on the rim; do not edit hands*. Cheap on phones: shared materials, a simpler low tier, no per-frame allocation, wheel triangles on high within about +40% of before. Nothing else in the cockpit changes. A regression check in tests/regression.mjs proves the new parts exist per car and the left dial updates when the profile changes. Earlier state: the wheel was built and the code lens KEPT it (33/33 incl. the new wheel check); the art lens's verdict was lost in the reset. PROVE: npx tsc --noEmit; npm run build (dist/artifact.html carries data-build="owner-test"); npm test -- --only=boot,phone,modes; seat-view frames with hands, Day and Night, 1280x720 and 390x844, for the GT, Corsa and Hypercar, one each for the Brio and Vela E, plus a close-up of the wheel (dials, pads, weave, stitching, stripe), with BEFORE frames from c3962c5 (build it in a scratch copy outside the worktree) into tests/out/sport-wheel/.
